Hana — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High level answers below; I added an attachment with a short technical note (karthik_quant_recs.pdf) that explains tradeoffs we typically recommend.

Credits model (short answer):
- Pilot credits are a blended unit that covers token generation and model runtime. For pilots we map credits to a conservative estimate of token-equivalent usage plus a small runtime buffer to cover peak bursts.
- Example: 1,000 pilot credits = ~100k generated tokens on a quantized runtime with batching; if you expect many long documents we size credits higher.

Quantization guardrails for mixed seq lengths:
- Short sequences (~<=256 tokens): INT8 provides near-lossless quality for many LLaMA/LLM variants; benefits are 2–3x perf gain.
- Long sequences (>1024 tokens): prefer mixed approach — keep attention/softmax in FP16 paths while quantizing feed-forward weights to INT8/4 where supported. This reduces KV cache growth and preserves generation fidelity.
- Always run your key eval prompts (we'll help with that) through INT8 and a fallback FP16 variant to measure regressions. We can automate canary evaluation across your prompt set.

Operational notes:
- Batching: we recommend conservative batch sizes for the pilot to preserve latency SLOs; the runtime supports continuous batching and adaptive thresholds that we can tune per endpoint.
- Caching: prefix caching for common templates (e.g., standard opening patient text) can cut token costs significantly; we can instrument cache hit rates in the Console during the pilot.

I'll outline a suggested commercial framing in a follow-up from Marissa (she handles credits/terms). Attached: karthik_quant_recs.pdf (technical appendix).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call next week to walk through the SOW + technical appendix.

— Karthik

Hana / Matt — appreciate the timeline. Quick commercial proposal aligned to the SOW:

Pilot structure (recommended):
- Integration tranche: 600 credits (covers integration + 1 week of dev testing).
- Evaluation tranche: 900 credits (covers 1 week of evaluation at a conservative 100k-token equivalent).
- Total pilot credits: 1,500 (we're flexible if Peregrine wants a different split).

Controls and safety valves: 
- Spend cap: we can gate evaluation tranche consumption with a hard cap and notify your team at 70% consumption. If you hit cap we'll pause generation until you authorize a top-up.
- FP16 fallback: yes — we can configure the same endpoint to automatically fallback to an FP16 variant if the canary checks detect more than a configurable regression threshold (default 2% absolute on your quality metric). That switch is seamless to your client.

Pricing and terms:
- Pilot credits are non-refundable but applied to future committed capacity if you convert within 60 days.
- For production commit, we can convert pilot credits into a 6–12 month committed discount at a negotiated conversion rate.

Attachments: a simple pilot pricing sheet (Pilot_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx) with a breakdown and an optional SOW clause we use for pilots.
